svg.title: 2027 Autonomous Navigation: data synthesis, VSLAM, and integration pipeline
svg.desc: Swimlane diagram of data synthesis, VSLAM, and integration across five phases (shared preflight, parallel subteam work, bundle validation, package conversion, GPS), listing each responsibility's inputs, outputs, functionality, dependencies, acceptance checks and exclusions, followed by the handoff bundle, contracts, and TF ownership chain.
svg.text: 2027 Autonomous Navigation · data synthesis, VSLAM, and integration · detailed pipeline
Short measurement preflight → data synthesis and VSLAM proceed in parallel → assemble one validated handoff bundle → package proven producers → GPS later.
Starting point: the standalone ZED prototype (main.py, slam/, object_detection.py)
Stays runnable as the replayable baseline. The ROS 2 workspace grows beside it; nothing is rewritten for folder neatness.
ZED stereo camera with IMU (RGB, depth, inertial data)
Optional SVO replay instead of the live camera
SVO recording, TUM trajectory text file, persisted ZED area map, YOLO overlays, depth-heuristic flags (walls, hallways, central obstacles, clusters)
ZED positional tracking with IMU fusion, depth retrieval, YOLO detection plus depth heuristics, plots of trajectory and displacement
No ROS 2 messages, no Nav2 map or costmap, no GPS, no motor commands. A ZED area map is not an OccupancyGrid.
A replay, plot or YOLO box proves a component ran, not that navigation is safe.
Where the work starts. The coloured chip says where the input comes from: LIVE = real hardware, FILE = recorded files or replay, SYNTHETIC = generated fixture,
What the box produces and hands onward: files, ROS topics, reports, contracts.
The main functionality, in the order it is built.
Dependencies. The chip names the source responsibility: DATA SYNTHESIS, VSLAM or INTEGRATION; TOOL = software or docs; EARLIER = previous phase; GATE = bundle
gate; NEXT TEAM = the downstream subteam.
Acceptance check: the claim may be made only when this is shown.
Deliberately out of scope for the box, to stop scope creep.

How responsibilities assemble the handoff bundle
Solid arrows are required handoffs; dashed purple is optional. Everyone is unblocked from day one by files, fixtures or synthetic messages.
standard messages, frame ids, rate, QoS
Confirms the bundle reads correctly at the gate
Topics and TF also reach the next subteam directly
Each handoff is a contract: who produces it, who consumes it, what fields it must carry, and when it is frozen.
Camera model, serial or anonymized id, resolution, FPS, intrinsics; coordinate convention and
base_link → camera_link transform; SVO and rosbag2 paths and checksums; start and end
timestamps, software versions, calibration version; tracking, IMU and GPS availability; route,
Standard message type, topic name, frame id, rate, QoS; one publisher per TF edge
Frame, resolution, occupancy and confidence, provenance
Obstacle source, TF and localization context, measured footprint, replay evidence, known
The one TF picture everyone must respect: map → odom → base_link → camera_link → imu_link
Only one component may publish each arrow. Two publishers for map → odom make the rover appear to jump and break navigation.
Exactly ONE owner, chosen at the integration gate.
Candidates: ZED tracking, SLAM Toolbox, AMCL, a GPS filter.
Local odometry: ZED camera+IMU tracking, or an external
filter only if real extra sensors exist. Wobbles documents
Anchor frame. Footprint is measured relative to it by

Static transform from the same URDF/xacro. GPS antenna frame
is added at the GPS stage.
Rules that hold across the whole timeline
No motors are commanded and no live motor command is an acceptance criterion; prove everything
through RViz, replay or simulation first.
This subteam hands inputs and evidence to the next subteam; that team builds costmaps and picks
GPS is last: a slow, noisy global correction, not a replacement for local camera motion.
VSLAM and integration can start without the IMU result.
All responsibilities need the final data-synthesis sensor, frame and manifest contracts for end-to-
The visual baseline and integration fixture are independent of the IMU result.
Every claim keeps its inputs, parameters, outputs and acceptance check so it can be reproduced.
Do not edit another person's package without agreement. Use standard ROS 2 message types at package
Generated SVO, rosbag2, maps, models and experiment outputs stay out of Git unless explicitly
